QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_9

question.text: Mr. Vijay, a foreign national (not an Indian citizen and not a PIO), visited India for 65 days in PY 2024-25, and his cumulative stay in India during the 4 preceding years was 400 days. Considering only the basic conditions for residency under section 6(1), what is his residential status — Resident or Non-Resident?

answer.text: Non-Resident, since he stayed less than 182 days in the previous year
Non-Resident, since the 60+365 test does not apply to foreign nationals
Resident, because he satisfies the 60-days-in-PY plus 365-days-in-4-preceding-years test
His Resident/Non-Resident status depends on whether his Indian income exceeds Rs. 15 lakh

explanation.text: The Logic: For foreign nationals who are NOT Indian citizens and NOT PIOs, the basic conditions for residency under s.6(1) are: (a) 182 or more days in the PY, OR (b) 60 or more days in the PY AND 365 or more days in the 4 preceding years. Mr. Vijay satisfies limb (b): 65 days (> 60) in PY 2024-25 and 400 days (> 365) in the 4 preceding years. He is therefore a Resident under the basic condition (option C). The Trap: Option A applies only the 182-day limb and ignores the 60+365 alternative. Option B incorrectly claims the 60+365 test does not apply to foreign nationals - it does. Option D drags in the Rs. 15 lakh threshold, which is part of the 120-day relaxation that applies only to Indian citizens and PIOs, not to other foreign nationals. In the original ambiguous version the stem asked for the full residential status (Resident/ROR/RNOR/NR) but the facts did not include the 9-of-10-year or 7-year-day-count data needed to distinguish ROR from RNOR. Note: The original was ambiguous because the four statutory categories are ROR, RNOR and NR, and the stem facts could not distinguish ROR from RNOR. The stem has been narrowed to only the Resident-vs-Non-Resident determination under the basic conditions, so option C is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series X-B (Investment Adviser Level 2), pp.139-141.
